mnemonic: The scroll rolls 巻 up and whatever was lying beside it goes in 込 with it. Your friend was standing too close: まきこむ.
notes: 関わる かかわる is being connected to a thing. 巻き込む is dragging somebody else into it with you.
sentence: 友達をトラブルに巻き込んでしまった。
sentence_meaning: I got my friend involved in the trouble.

mnemonic: The hand comes out 出 from under the cuff and then stays out there, waiting. He wanted to shake on it: さしだす.
sentence: 彼は握手をしようと手を差し出したの。
sentence_meaning: He put out his hand to shake hands.

mnemonic: Carts drawn up in rows with covers over them and everybody who came along with them. The wounded went to their hospital: ぐん.
sentence: 怪我人は軍の病院に運ばれたよ。
sentence_meaning: The injured were taken to the army hospital.

mnemonic: Not here and not over there, the way you happen to be standing. I will be with you by the evening: そちら.
notes: The polite one. そっち is casual and そこ is the plain there. Same set as こちら and あちら.
sentence: 夕方そちらに着きます。
sentence_meaning: I'll arrive there in the evening.

mnemonic: The heart 忄 goes over the losing goal every 毎 time you shut your eyes, and the match was two days ago: くやしい.
notes: 後悔 こうかい is regret at something you did. 悔しい is the sting of having lost or been beaten.
sentence: 試合に負けてとても悔しい。
sentence_meaning: I'm so frustrated that we lost the game.

mnemonic: You get a grip on it and the whole thing comes away in your hand, cork and all, and the bottle is open: ぬく.
notes: 取り出す とりだす is taking a thing out of somewhere. 抜く is pulling it free of whatever was holding it.
sentence: ワインのコルクを抜きました。
sentence_meaning: I uncorked the wine.

mnemonic: Stone 石 through skin 皮, and then the ground 壊 itself goes back to being ground. It is happening to the countryside: はかい.
sentence: 自然の破壊が進んでいるのよ。
sentence_meaning: The destruction of nature is advancing.

mnemonic: Your life 命 gets carried 運 down a road you had no part in picking, and arguing with it has never worked for anybody: うんめい.
sentence: 運命には逆らえないよ。
sentence_meaning: You can't go against fate.

mnemonic: You take somebody inside 内 the plan 案 of the place you already carry in your head, and walk them round it. Kyoto, all day: あんない.
sentence: 京都を案内します。
sentence_meaning: I will show you Kyoto.

mnemonic: A servant's 奴 power 力, which is the kind you have to keep putting in rather than the kind you have. Try harder: どりょく.
sentence: もっと努力しよう。
sentence_meaning: Let's try harder.

mnemonic: No date, no arrangement, and both of you mean it anyway. We will run into each other again at some point: いずれ.
sentence: いずれまたお会いしましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's meet again sometime.

mnemonic: One 一 word 言, which is exactly what you ask the president for when you actually want five minutes: ひとこと.
sentence: 社長に一言お願いしたの。
sentence_meaning: I asked the president to say a few words.

mnemonic: Four attempts and three years, and the letter has finally come. The end of a long road rather than a short one: ついに.
notes: やっと and ようやく do the same job. ついに leans on the length of what came before, and it works for bad endings too. At last is not at least: せめて and 少なくとも are at least.
sentence: 彼はついに弁護士の資格を取ったよ。
sentence_meaning: He finally passed the bar examination.

mnemonic: The heart 心 as the organ stored away 臓 in there doing the pumping, not the one you fall in love with. Hers is not well: しんぞう.
notes: 心 こころ is the heart you feel things with. 心臓 is the one a doctor puts a stethoscope on.
sentence: 祖母は心臓が悪いんだ。
sentence_meaning: My grandmother has a heart condition.

mnemonic: Whatever 何 the thing 物 is, it is in a box now and it is going to his house. Handle it gently on the way: にもつ.
sentence: 彼の家に荷物を送りました。
sentence_meaning: I sent a package to his house.

mnemonic: A person 亻 reaching up and then carrying on reaching, and it turns out your hair has been at the same thing for months: のびる.
sentence: 髪がだいぶ伸びたね。
sentence_meaning: Your hair has grown a lot, hasn't it?

mnemonic: Both 両 of the ones who stood up on the tree to see further 親, in the same room, being introduced to your girlfriend: りょうしん.
sentence: 両親に彼女を紹介した。
sentence_meaning: I introduced my girlfriend to my parents.

mnemonic: Somebody has weighed it and there is a great deal of it. The spaghetti in that place turns up in a bucket: りょう.
sentence: この店のスパゲッティは量が多いです。
sentence_meaning: This restaurant's spaghetti portions are big.

mnemonic: Your own 厶 hand 扌 goes out with the money sitting on it, and the argument at the end of a meal is over who does that: はらう.
sentence: 私が払いましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let me pay for that.

mnemonic: Not a second 二 time 度, not ever. He is walking out of the door and telling you he will not be back: にどと.
notes: Always with a negative later in the sentence: 二度と来ません, I will never come here again.
sentence: もうここには二度と来ません。
sentence_meaning: I'll never come here again.

mnemonic: The ground lying either side of where you are stood, taken in with one turn of the head. We had a look round: あたり.
notes: Near 当たり あたり, a hit, in sound. 周り まわり is what is around a thing. 辺り is roughly here.
sentence: 辺りを見回したの。
sentence_meaning: We looked around the area.

mnemonic: The gate opens 開 and the thing begins 始, and both halves of the word say so. Sports day starts at nine: かいし.
notes: 最初 さいしょ is the first part of something and 始め はじめ is the beginning of it. 開始 is the moment it starts, and it is the one that goes with a time.
sentence: 運動会は9時開始です。
sentence_meaning: The sports festival meet begins at nine o'clock.

mnemonic: Untie 解 the thing first and then let go 放 of it, which is two separate kindnesses. They let the hostage walk: かいほう.
sentence: 人質が解放されてよかった。
sentence_meaning: It is good that the hostage has been freed.

mnemonic: The go-between 仲 part of it is good 良, which is the whole of what getting on with somebody amounts to. That couple manage it: なかよく.
sentence: あの夫婦は仲良く暮らしているよ。
sentence_meaning: That married couple is living happily together.

mnemonic: The wild sort, the kind you would want a weapon for, and not the one asleep on the sofa. He had eyes like one: けもの.
sentence: 彼は獣のような目をしていたな。
sentence_meaning: He had eyes like a beast.

meaning: to come off, to be removed
mnemonic: Nobody took 取 it off. It took itself off, and the button is somewhere on the floor of the train: とれる.
sentence: シャツのボタンが取れた。
sentence_meaning: My shirt's button came off.

mnemonic: A thing 物 that was put up 建 in order to stand there, and this one has been standing longer than any other in the country: たてもの.
sentence: これは日本一古い建物です。
sentence_meaning: This is the oldest building in Japan.

mnemonic: What came 来 out of the root 本 of the thing before anything got piled on top of it. The pressure lifted and there she was again: ほんらい.
sentence: 彼女はプレッシャーから解放されて本来の自分に戻ったな。
sentence_meaning: She was relieved of the pressure and went back to her original self.

mnemonic: It is in your hands now, and how it comes out the far end is entirely down to you. That box has glass in it: あつかう.
sentence: この荷物は丁寧に扱ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please handle this luggage carefully.

mnemonic: A true 真 face 面 and a straight eye 目, three characters all saying the same thing about the man. He means it: まじめ.
notes: 真剣 しんけん is being in earnest about one particular thing. 真面目 is what somebody is like all the time.
sentence: 彼は真面目な人です。
sentence_meaning: He's a serious-minded person.

mnemonic: A shadow 影 of him and an echo 響 of him, both still going long after he has left the room. That is what he did to me: えいきょう.
notes: 効果 こうか is the effect a thing has. 影響 is the mark somebody or something leaves on you.
sentence: 私は彼から大きな影響を受けました。
sentence_meaning: I was deeply influenced by him.

mnemonic: True 真 red 赤 with nothing else mixed into it, and his whole face had gone that colour: まっか.
sentence: 彼の顔は真っ赤でした。
sentence_meaning: His face was red.

mnemonic: Something goes off 発 and somebody sees 見 it for the first time anybody has. A new star, last night: はっけん.
sentence: 新しい星が発見された。
sentence_meaning: A new star was discovered.

mnemonic: A hand 又 underneath taking the whole weight, and it does not get to put the thing down. That is his father's job: ささえる.
sentence: 父親には一家を支える責任がある。
sentence_meaning: My father has the responsibility to support the family.

mnemonic: Whatever else is on the list, this is the one sitting at the top of it. Work, ahead of everything: だいいち.
notes: 最初 さいしょ is first in time, the beginning of a thing. 第一 is first in importance.
sentence: 私には仕事が第一です。
sentence_meaning: Work is my first priority.

mnemonic: The one with the axe 父, with お on the front and さん on the end because you are talking to him rather than about him: おとうさん.
notes: 父 ちち is your own father when you mention him to somebody else. お父さん is what you call him, and the word for anybody else's.
sentence: お父さんは会社員です。
sentence_meaning: My father's a company employee.

mnemonic: The same お and さん wrapped round 母, and the one being talked about here belongs to somebody else, and she is a beauty: おかあさん.
notes: 母 はは is your own mother when you mention her to others. お母さん is what you call her, and the word for anybody else's.
sentence: 彼のお母さんは美人です。
sentence_meaning: His mother is a beauty.

mnemonic: The big brother 兄 with the polite wrapping put back on. How old is yours: おにいさん.
notes: 兄 あに is your own older brother when you talk about him. お兄さん is what you call him, and anybody else's.
sentence: あなたのお兄さんは何歳？
sentence_meaning: How old is your big brother?

mnemonic: The big sister 姉 done up politely, and the one you ran into yesterday was somebody else's: おねえさん.
notes: 姉 あね is your own older sister when you talk about her. お姉さん is what you call her, and anybody else's.
sentence: 昨日、あなたのお姉さんに会ったよ。
sentence_meaning: I met your older sister yesterday.

mnemonic: Your parent's brother, and the same word does duty for any middle-aged man whose name you have not been given: おじさん.
notes: One long vowel from おじいさん, grandfather. Short is the uncle and long is the grandfather, and おばさん and おばあさん split the same way.
sentence: 昨日おじさんに会いました。
sentence_meaning: I met my uncle yesterday.

mnemonic: Your parent's sister, arriving with her whole family behind her and settling in for the afternoon: おばさん.
notes: One long vowel from おばあさん, grandmother. Short is the aunt and long is the grandmother.
sentence: おばさん一家が遊びに来ました。
sentence_meaning: My aunt and her family came to visit me.

mnemonic: Your aunt's child, born the same year as you, and the only relative you have anything at all in common with: いとこ.
sentence: いとこと私は同じ年です。
sentence_meaning: My cousin and I are the same age.

mnemonic: Somebody bought it for you and now the homework has nowhere left to hide. Four legs, one flat surface: つくえ.
sentence: 新しい机を買ってもらいました。
sentence_meaning: I was bought a new desk.

meaning: of the same kind, each other, fellow
mnemonic: Two of the same 同 sort stood together, and he and I turn out to be cousins on both sides of it: どうし.
notes: お互い おたがい is each other as in mutually, what two people do to one another. 同士 tags two of the same kind.
sentence: 彼と私はいとこ同士です。
sentence_meaning: He and I are fellow cousins.

mnemonic: Whatever was in front of you went at its own pace and the gap opened up behind it. She got to school after the bell: おくれる.
sentence: 今朝彼女は学校に遅れました。
sentence_meaning: She was late for school this morning.

mnemonic: Two wheels and the bar between them, drawn from directly overhead. His younger brother has just bought one: くるま.
sentence: 弟が車を買った。
sentence_meaning: My younger brother bought a car.

mnemonic: Wings 飛 up and straight out 出 through the doorway without looking first, and the road was right there: とびだす.
sentence: 彼は道路に飛び出したの。
sentence_meaning: He ran out into the road.

mnemonic: The affair 事 and the state 態 it has managed to get itself into, and this one has got into a bad one: じたい.
notes: 状況 じょうきょう is the situation as circumstances. 事態 is the state a matter has reached, and it is usually grave. Near 時代 じだい in sound.
sentence: 事態は深刻です。
sentence_meaning: The situation is serious.

mnemonic: Somebody facing the same way 方 as you with the same taste 味 in a fight. Your mother, every single time: みかた.
notes: 友達 ともだち and 友人 ゆうじん are friends. 味方 is about whose side somebody is on.
sentence: 母はいつも私の味方です。
sentence_meaning: My mother will always be my ally.

mnemonic: The thing gets laid out 展 and opened up 開 as it goes along, and the story got away from you three turns back: てんかい.
sentence: 話の展開についていけない。
sentence_meaning: I can't follow the thread of the conversation.
